metadata.title: The Pharaoh's Architect
metadata.description: You fell through a crumbling floor into the sealed lower chambers of Pharaoh Khufu-Ankh's tomb. Above, the passage has collapsed. Below, Khepri — an ancient mechanical guardian of bronze and obsidian — patrols the corridors, its clockwork gears clicking in the darkness. Navigate ten chambers of ingenious ancient engineering to reach the hidden exit before Khepri finds you.
metadata.author: ai-generated

setting.ambient_text: Dust motes drift in faint light filtering from cracks above. The air is stale — sealed for millennia. Somewhere in the darkness, gears click rhythmically. Something is moving.

items.name: Clay Shard
items.description: A curved pottery fragment with faded hieratic script.

then.text: Hieratic text — a cursive form of hieroglyphs. You can make out numerals: 3, 7, 1, 4, 9. A code?

items.name: Copper Chisel
items.description: A sturdy copper chisel, still sharp after millennia.

then.text: Solid copper with a wooden handle. The architect's personal tool — his cartouche is stamped on the handle.

items.name: Linen Strip
items.description: A long strip of burial linen, surprisingly strong.

then.text: Fine weave, still flexible. About two meters long. Useful for wrapping, binding, or as a fuse.

items.name: Bronze Gear
items.description: A small precision gear, clearly part of a larger mechanism.

then.text: Twelve teeth, precisely machined. The same alloy as Khepri's joints. This could repair — or sabotage — mechanical systems.

items.name: Architect's Papyrus
items.description: A rolled papyrus with detailed technical drawings.

then.text: The architect's personal notes. Diagrams of the water system, the observatory lens alignment, and — crucially — the location of a hidden passage behind the workshop wall. A notation reads: 'The exit requires five seals. The worthy find them. The unworthy feed Khepri.'

items.name: Crystal Lens
items.description: A polished quartz lens that refracts light into rainbows.

then.text: Polished to perfection. When you hold it up, hidden UV-reactive pigments on nearby surfaces might glow. The ancient Egyptians knew more about optics than we thought.
You rotate the lens. Light bends through it in unexpected ways. This could reveal hidden markings.

items.name: Golden Scarab Amulet
items.description: A heavy gold scarab with lapis lazuli inlays. It functions as a key.

then.text: The underside has a unique tooth pattern — a key for scarab-shaped locks. The wings are slightly loose, as if designed to open.
You pry the wings apart. Inside: a tiny rolled papyrus with star coordinates. Sirius at zenith, Orion at 15 degrees.

items.name: Feather of Ma'at
items.description: An ostrich feather, perfectly preserved, gold-tipped.

then.text: The feather of truth. In mythology, your heart is weighed against it. Light as air, yet it holds the weight of judgment.

items.name: Heart Scarab
items.description: A green stone scarab inscribed with a spell from the Book of the Dead.

then.text: Chapter 30B of the Book of the Dead: 'O my heart, do not stand as a witness against me.' Placed on the heart during judgment to ensure it does not betray the deceased's sins.

items.name: Architect's Compass
items.description: A bronze drawing compass with adjustable legs.

then.text: One leg ends in a sharp point — sharp enough to scratch metal or score stone. The pivot joint is the same alloy as Khepri's gears.

items.name: Reed Pen
items.description: A sharpened reed with residual ink.

then.text: Still has dried ink. With water, it could write again.

items.name: Sacred Oil Flask
items.description: A small alabaster flask containing ancient lamp oil, still volatile.

then.text: Cedar oil mixed with natron. Still combustible after millennia — the seal was airtight. Enough to fill a channel or fuel a fire.

items.name: Bronze Mirror
items.description: A polished bronze hand mirror with a lotus handle.

then.text: Your reflection stares back, distorted by millennia of tarnish. But it still reflects light well enough to redirect a beam.

items.name: Cartouche Seal — Khufu-Ankh
items.description: A stone cartouche bearing the pharaoh's name.

then.text: The royal name in a protective oval. One of five seals needed for the exit door.

items.name: Cartouche Seal — Imhotep
items.description: A stone cartouche bearing the architect god's name.

then.text: Imhotep — patron of architects. The second of five seals.

items.name: Cartouche Seal — Thoth
items.description: A stone cartouche bearing the knowledge god's name.

then.text: Thoth — lord of wisdom and writing. The third of five seals.

items.name: Cartouche Seal — Ma'at
items.description: A stone cartouche bearing the truth goddess's name.

then.text: Ma'at — goddess of truth and balance. The fourth of five seals.

items.name: Cartouche Seal — Ra
items.description: A stone cartouche bearing the sun god's name.

then.text: Ra — the sun. The fifth and final seal. With all five, the exit door can be opened.

items.name: Copper Wire
items.description: A thin coil of copper wire, pulled from the forge.

then.text: Thin, flexible, conductive. Could be used to bypass a mechanism or set a tripwire trap.

items.name: Fine Sand
items.description: A pouch of very fine sand from the timer device.

then.text: Incredibly fine-grained. Could be used to jam gears, fill a channel, or track footprints.

items.name: Golden Ushabti
items.description: A small golden servant figure, heavy and valuable.

then.text: An ushabti — a servant for the afterlife. Solid gold, incredibly heavy for its size. The base is engraved: 'I shall answer for the Pharaoh in the place of labor.'

items.name: Ivory Wand
items.description: A curved hippo-ivory wand with protective deities carved along its length.

then.text: An apotropaic wand — used to draw protective circles. The curve is exactly the radius of Khepri's sensor range. The ancients measured the guardian's reach.

items.name: Natron Pouch
items.description: A leather pouch of natron — natural drying salt used in mummification.

then.text: Sodium carbonate crystals. Absorbs moisture, preserves organic material, and — importantly — is abrasive enough to corrode bronze joints.

items.name: Oil-Soaked Fuse
items.description: A strip of linen soaked in lamp oil, ready to burn.

then.text: The oil has saturated the linen completely. It would catch fire instantly.

items.name: Sabotaged Gear
items.description: A bronze gear clogged with fine sand, designed to jam machinery.

then.text: The sand grains are lodged deep between the teeth. Any mechanism using this would grind to a halt.

items.name: Tripwire Trap
items.description: Copper wire strung between bronze gear anchors, nearly invisible.

then.text: A simple but effective trap. Anyone walking through would catch their ankle.

items.name: Corrosive Paste
items.description: A caustic mixture of natron and oil that dissolves soft metals.

then.text: The paste bubbles slightly. Ancient Egyptian embalmers used natron to dissolve flesh — this would eat through bronze fittings.

items.name: Light Redirector
items.description: A crystal lens mounted on a bronze mirror frame, focusing light into a beam.

then.text: By combining the lens and mirror, you have created a device that can redirect and focus sunlight or lamplight.

items.name: Forged Decree
items.description: A papyrus scroll bearing a convincing replica of a royal decree.

then.text: Written in your best approximation of hieratic script, sealed with the cartouche seal. It declares this tomb sealed by royal authority.

items.name: Precision Tool
items.description: The architect's compass fitted with a copper chisel tip, perfect for fine stone work.

then.text: The compass provides steady guidance while the chisel does the cutting. Together they can carve with incredible precision.

combinations.message: You soak the linen strip in sacred oil. A slow-burning fuse.
You pack fine sand into the gear teeth. When inserted into any mechanism, it will grind and seize.
You fashion a tripwire with the gear as an anchor. Khepri's legs would catch on this.
You mix natron with oil into a thick paste. This would eat through bronze joints over time.
You mount the lens in front of the mirror. Together, they can focus and redirect any light beam with precision.
Using the architect's own pen and papyrus, you carefully copy the cartouche style. You write a 'royal decree' ordering Khepri to stand down. Whether the automaton can read is another question.
The compass guides the chisel for precise cuts. Together, you can carve stone or pick locks with surgical accuracy.

objects.name: Collapsed Ceiling
objects.description: The hole you fell through. Rubble blocks the way back up.

then.text: Tons of limestone rubble. You're not going back that way. The only path is forward — deeper into the tomb.
You shift a few stones. More cascade down. It's hopelessly blocked.

objects.name: Rubble Pile
objects.description: Broken stone and debris from the ceiling collapse.

then.text: A mound of broken stone. Something glints between the rocks — pottery shards, a piece of copper.
You dig through the rubble. A clay shard with writing, and a copper chisel — must have fallen with you from the upper level.
Broken stones and dust. You've already salvaged what you could.

objects.name: Wall Torch Sconce
objects.description: An iron bracket holding a pitch-soaked torch.

then.text: An ancient torch. The pitch is dry but might still catch. You'd need a spark.
You pull it from the bracket but can't light it with bare hands.
You strike the chisel against the stone wall. Sparks fly. The pitch catches — firelight floods the chamber, revealing hieroglyphs covering every surface.
The torch burns steadily, casting dancing shadows. The walls are alive with hieroglyphs.

objects.name: Stone Door (North)
objects.description: A massive stone slab with a carved scarab in the center.

then.text: A massive stone door. A scarab-shaped depression in the center — a keyhole of sorts. Beyond this lies the Hall of Pillars.
Immovable. The scarab lock must be the key.
The golden scarab clicks into place. Ancient gears grind beneath the floor. The stone slab slides sideways, revealing a pillared hall beyond.
You carefully pick the scarab lock with the compass-guided chisel. It takes patience, but the mechanism yields. The door grinds open.

objects.name: Hieroglyph Wall
objects.description: The chamber walls are covered in carved and painted hieroglyphs.

then.text: Intricate carvings cover the wall. You can see a map, warnings, and what appears to be the architect's personal notes. Worth a closer look.

objects.name: Clay Jars
objects.description: A cluster of sealed clay storage jars.

then.text: Storage jars for the afterlife. Seals are intact — preserved for thousands of years.
You crack open a jar. Inside: sacred oil in an alabaster flask, still sealed. Another contains natron salt in a leather pouch.
Broken jars. You've taken everything useful.

objects.name: Fallen Pillar
objects.description: A toppled column, creating a sheltered space beneath.

then.text: A massive stone column, toppled and cracked. The gap beneath is just large enough to squeeze into — a hiding spot if Khepri comes.
You crawl under the pillar. Dark, cramped, but hidden from view.

objects.name: Sand Drift
objects.description: Wind-blown sand that has accumulated in the corner.

then.text: Fine desert sand, accumulated over centuries through cracks above.
You scoop fine sand into your pouch.

objects.name: Wall Alcove
objects.description: A small recess in the wall, partially hidden by rubble.

then.text: A dark niche in the wall, partly blocked by fallen stone. Something glints inside.
You clear the rubble. Inside the niche: a golden scarab amulet on a stone pedestal, glowing faintly in the torchlight.

objects.name: Scarab Pedestal
objects.description: A small stone pedestal holding a golden scarab.

then.text: You lift the golden scarab. It's heavy, warm to the touch. The scarab depression on the north door suddenly makes sense.
A golden scarab amulet rests on the pedestal. Lapis lazuli wings, obsidian eyes. It looks like it would fit the door's lock perfectly.

objects.name: Cartouche Panel
objects.description: A panel of royal cartouches — names of pharaohs.

then.text: Royal names in oval frames. You recognize Khufu-Ankh — the pharaoh entombed here. Below his name: five smaller cartouches representing the gods who guard the exit.

Through the lens, hidden pigments fluoresce! Between the cartouches, invisible text appears: 'The worthy pass through knowledge, craft, and truth. The five seals open only for one who has walked all chambers.' A map of the seal locations glows faintly.

objects.name: Warning Inscription
objects.description: Carved warnings flanking the doorway.

then.text: 'He who disturbs the Pharaoh's rest shall face Khepri, the Scarab Who Walks. It does not sleep. It does not tire. It hears the dust settle.'
You read the warning aloud. The words echo. From deep in the tomb, you hear a mechanical click-click-click, as if something acknowledged your voice.

objects.name: Map Carving
objects.description: A carved layout of the tomb complex.

then.text: A floor plan of the tomb! Ten chambers connected by corridors. The Antechamber (you are here) leads north to the Hall of Pillars, which branches east and west. The exit corridor is marked at the far end, past the Treasury. Five seal symbols are marked at different chambers.

objects.name: Architect's Signature
objects.description: A small personal cartouche, different from the royal ones.

then.text: 'Designed by Senenmut, Royal Architect. May the worthy find my workshop and learn the secrets I built into these walls. The unworthy will not leave.' A personal message from the man who built this death trap.
Hidden ink fluoresces: 'My workshop is behind the fourth pillar in the Hall. Press the architect's mark — my compass — three times.' A hidden passage hint!

objects.name: Left Pillar Row
objects.description: Four massive stone pillars with carved reliefs.

then.text: Four pillars carved with scenes of daily life — farmers, builders, scribes. The fourth pillar has a compass symbol at its base, different from the rest.
You press the compass mark on the fourth pillar three times. Click. Click. Click. A section of wall behind the pillar grinds open, revealing a dusty workshop!
You run your hands along the carved reliefs. Beautiful craftsmanship. The compass symbol on the fourth pillar is slightly raised, like a button, but you're not sure what to do with it.

objects.name: Right Pillar Row
objects.description: Four matching pillars on the right side.

then.text: Four pillars with carved scenes of the afterlife — judgment, the Field of Reeds, the sun's journey. Between them, deep shadows offer concealment.

objects.name: Ceiling Light Shaft
objects.description: A narrow shaft in the ceiling letting in a beam of light.

then.text: A narrow shaft cut through solid rock to the surface. A beam of sunlight streams down, illuminating dust motes. Too narrow to climb through, but the light itself might be useful — if redirected.

You position the lens-mirror assembly in the light beam. The focused beam can now be directed anywhere in the hall — including into the connecting corridors where it might activate light-sensitive mechanisms!
You hold the mirror in the beam. It reflects, but without a lens the beam is too diffuse to do anything useful at distance.

objects.name: Floor Pressure Plate
objects.description: A slightly raised stone tile in the center of the hall.

then.text: A pressure plate. Step on it and Khepri will know exactly where you are. The ancient builders used these as an alarm system.
You press it with your hand. A loud click echoes through the corridors. Somewhere, Khepri changes direction.
You pour fine sand into the mechanism beneath the plate, jamming the gears. The plate sinks slightly and locks in place — disabled.
You wedge the sand-packed gear into the plate mechanism. It seizes instantly — permanently disabled.

objects.name: East Passage
objects.description: An open archway leading east to the Scarab Chamber.

then.text: An archway leading east. You can see the shimmer of gold and lapis lazuli — the Scarab Chamber.
You pass through the archway into the Scarab Chamber.

objects.name: West Passage
objects.description: An open archway leading west to the Weighing Room.

then.text: An archway leading west. Beyond, you glimpse the glint of a massive bronze scale — the Weighing Room of Ma'at.
You enter the Weighing Room.

objects.name: South Passage (to Antechamber)
objects.description: The archway back to the Antechamber.

then.text: You return to the Antechamber.

objects.name: Shadow Alcove
objects.description: A dark recess between two pillars.

then.text: Deep shadow between the pillars. You could press yourself flat against the wall here and be nearly invisible.
You press into the shadow. The stone is cold against your back. Hidden.

objects.name: Oil Channel
objects.description: A shallow stone channel running along the base of the walls.

then.text: A shallow stone channel running the perimeter of the hall. Ancient lamp fuel channels. They connect to channels in every adjacent room.
You pour the sacred oil into the channel. It flows slowly along the perimeter, filling the ancient fuel channels. Now, if ignited...

You light the fuse and touch it to the oil. WHOOSH! Fire races through the channels, lighting sconces throughout the connected chambers. The tomb blazes with light — and the flames create a temporary barrier in the corridors. Khepri won't cross fire.

effects.text: The oil fires burn low. The corridors are passable again — for you and Khepri both.

objects.name: Workshop Entrance
objects.description: A hidden doorway behind the fourth pillar.

then.text: You step through into the architect's personal workshop. Dust hangs thick. No one has entered this room in over three thousand years.

objects.name: Creation Myth Relief
objects.description: Carved scenes depicting the Egyptian creation myth.

then.text: The primordial waters of Nun. Atum emerging. The separation of sky and earth. Beautiful work — and between the scenes, a numerical sequence: the positions of stars at creation. This is the code for the observatory alignment.

objects.name: Number Sequence
objects.description: Hieratic numerals carved in a deliberate pattern.

then.text: A sequence of hieratic numerals: 5 - 3 - 7 - 2. Below them, a drawing of a chest with a keyhole shaped like a scarab.

objects.name: Star Map Fragment
objects.description: A partial map of the night sky carved into the pillar.

then.text: Orion, Sirius, the Pleiades — the stars the Egyptians used to align their monuments. Markings indicate specific angles. This matches what would be needed for the Observatory.

objects.name: Builder's Prayer
objects.description: A personal prayer carved by a worker.

then.text: 'I, Menna, carved these pillars for forty seasons. I pray to Ptah: let my hands be remembered. If you read this, stranger, know that men like me built this wonder. Not slaves — craftsmen.' A poignant message from across the ages.
You whisper: 'Your hands are remembered, Menna. I see your work.' The silence of three millennia answers back.

objects.name: Scarab Mosaic Floor
objects.description: An intricate floor mosaic depicting a giant scarab.

then.text: A massive scarab mosaic — lapis lazuli, carnelian, turquoise, and gold. The wings, sun disc, and eye are each distinct sections. It looks like a puzzle.

objects.name: Jeweled Scarab Statue
objects.description: A large scarab statue of polished black stone.

then.text: An obsidian scarab the size of a dog. Its eyes are red garnets. At its feet, a small basin and an inscription: 'Feed the scarab, and the golden door shall open.'

You place the golden ushabti in the basin. The statue's eyes flash. The golden door behind it begins to grind open — the treasure room awaits. But using a priceless artifact as tribute... the moral weight lingers.

You place the heart scarab in the basin. The statue's eyes glow blue. Instead of the golden door, a hidden panel in the wall slides open — a passage directly to the Observatory! The scholarly path reveals a shortcut.

objects.name: Offering Basin
objects.description: A stone basin at the base of the scarab statue.

then.text: An offering basin. What you place here determines which path opens — the treasure route or the knowledge route.

objects.name: Wall Slots
objects.description: Rectangular slots carved into the wall in a grid pattern.

then.text: A grid of narrow slots. They look like they could hold cartouche seals. An inscription reads: 'Place the seals of passage here.'

objects.name: Golden Door
objects.description: A door sheathed in gold leaf.

then.text: Sheathed in gold. Beyond lies the Treasury. The scarab statue seems to control this door.
Locked. The scarab statue controls the mechanism.
You step through the golden door into the Treasury.

objects.name: Sand Timer Mechanism
objects.description: An enormous bronze hourglass connected to the floor mechanism.

then.text: A giant bronze hourglass. When flipped, sand flows through for about 60 seconds. A mechanism connects it to the floor mosaic — starting the timer might activate the mosaic puzzle, but it also makes considerable noise.
You flip the massive hourglass. Bronze gears engage. Sand begins to flow. The floor mosaic comes alive — tiles can now be pressed in sequence. You have about 60 seconds.

effects.text: The sand runs out. The mosaic tiles lock in place.

objects.name: Ceiling Mirror
objects.description: A polished bronze disc mounted on the ceiling.

then.text: A polished bronze disc on the ceiling. It reflects the mosaic floor below — and from this angle, you can see that certain tiles are slightly raised, forming a pattern invisible from floor level. The wings, sun disc, and eye must be pressed in the right order!

objects.name: Hidden Passage to Observatory
objects.description: A narrow passage revealed by the knowledge offering.

then.text: You squeeze through the narrow passage. It opens into a vast chamber — the Observatory. Stars are painted on the ceiling, and a complex lens apparatus sits at the center.

objects.name: Left Wing Tile
objects.description: The left wing section of the scarab mosaic.

then.text: You press the left wing tile. It sinks slightly with a click.
The tile doesn't move. The sand timer mechanism must be activated first.

objects.name: Right Wing Tile
objects.description: The right wing section of the scarab mosaic.

then.text: You press the right wing tile. Click.

objects.name: Sun Disc Tile
objects.description: The central sun disc of the scarab mosaic.

then.text: You press the golden sun disc. It sinks with a satisfying click.

objects.name: Eye of Horus Tile
objects.description: The Eye of Horus at the center of the scarab.

then.text: You press the Eye of Horus. The final click. The entire mosaic shudders and sinks a few inches, revealing a hidden compartment beneath the scarab's body.
Inside the compartment: the first cartouche seal — Khufu-Ankh, the Pharaoh himself.

objects.name: Gear Assembly
objects.description: Exposed bronze gears beneath the mosaic floor.

then.text: Interlocking bronze gears — the mechanism that powers the mosaic puzzle and the sand timer. Remarkably similar to Khepri's internal workings. A spare gear could be taken.
You carefully extract a small gear without disrupting the mechanism.

objects.name: Bronze Lever
objects.description: A heavy lever connected to the counterweight system.

then.text: You throw the lever. Counterweights shift. The sand timer resets — you can run the mosaic puzzle again if needed.

objects.name: Sand Channel
objects.description: The channel that feeds sand to the timer.

then.text: Fine sand flows through this channel into the hourglass mechanism. The same fine sand that's drifted into the Antechamber.

objects.name: Counterweight Chain
objects.description: A bronze chain connecting to counterweights below.

then.text: Heavy bronze chain. The counterweight system is what powers many of the tomb's mechanical doors and traps.
You pull a thin copper wire from the chain's binding. It was used to secure the links.

objects.name: Scales of Ma'at
objects.description: A massive bronze balance scale, perfectly preserved.

then.text: The Scales of Ma'at — where the dead's heart is weighed against the feather of truth. The right pan holds a stone heart. The left pan is empty, awaiting the feather. An Anubis statue watches with jackal eyes.

objects.name: Feather Pedestal
objects.description: An empty pedestal where the Feather of Ma'at should rest.

then.text: An empty pedestal. The feather-shaped impression suggests the Feather of Ma'at was kept here once.

objects.name: Heart Jar Shelf
objects.description: Shelves of canopic jars — the heart jar is prominent.

then.text: Four canopic jars — one for each organ. The heart jar, topped with a human head (Imsety), is larger than the others. A heart scarab amulet rests beside it.
You take the heart scarab. The Anubis statue's eyes seem to follow you.

objects.name: Anubis Statue
objects.description: A life-sized Anubis with obsidian eyes that seem to watch you.

then.text: The jackal-headed god of the dead. Its obsidian eyes track movement — not supernatural, just clever engineering with weighted irises. It 'watches' whoever approaches the scales.

messages: You whisper to the statue: 'Judge me worthy.' The obsidian eyes stare back, unblinking.
You address Anubis: 'I seek passage, not treasure.' The silence is your only answer.
You speak the traditional plea: 'My heart is true.' The chamber echoes your words back at you.

objects.name: Judgment Door
objects.description: The door beyond the scales, leading deeper into the tomb.

then.text: Sealed. An inscription: 'Only the judged may pass.' The scales must be balanced first.
You pass through the Judgment Door into the Burial Chamber.

objects.name: Confession Tablet
objects.description: A stone tablet inscribed with the Negative Confessions.

then.text: The 42 Negative Confessions — 'I have not stolen, I have not killed, I have not lied...' The scale of Ma'at requires truth. The feather must be placed on the left pan while speaking a confession.
You read the confessions aloud. Your voice fills the chamber with three-thousand-year-old words of moral accounting. The Anubis statue's eyes track you slowly.

objects.name: Soul Jars
objects.description: A collection of small sealed jars with hieratic labels.

then.text: Small jars labeled with names. Previous 'visitors' to the tomb? Or symbolic representations? One is labeled with a feather glyph.
You open the feather-labeled jar. Inside: a perfectly preserved ostrich feather, gold-tipped. The Feather of Ma'at.

objects.name: Left Scale Pan
objects.description: The left pan of the scales — empty.

then.text: You place the feather on the left pan and speak: 'My heart is true. I seek only passage.' The scales tilt... teeter... and balance perfectly. The needle rests at center. A deep clunk echoes as the Judgment Door unlocks.
A compartment opens in the Anubis statue's base. Inside: the fourth cartouche seal — Ma'at.
You place the feather on the pan. The scales tip but don't balance. Something is missing — you must speak the confessions first. The feather lifts back to you.

objects.name: Right Scale Pan
objects.description: The right pan holds a stone heart.

then.text: A carved stone heart sits in the right pan. It represents the heart of the deceased, heavy with deeds — both good and bad.

objects.name: Balance Needle
objects.description: The central needle indicating the scale's balance.

then.text: The needle tilts right — the heart side is heavy. The feather pan is empty.
The needle rests perfectly center. Judgment is passed. You may proceed.

objects.name: Calibration Weights
objects.description: A set of bronze calibration weights.

then.text: Calibration weights for the scales. Trying to cheat the scales with extra weight would be... unwise. The Anubis statue seems to be watching.

You try to add the golden ushabti to the feather pan to force a balance. The Anubis statue's head rotates with a mechanical snap. Wrong move. The scales crash together and an alarm bell rings deep in the tomb.

objects.name: Sarcophagus
objects.description: The massive stone sarcophagus of Pharaoh Khufu-Ankh.

then.text: The massive stone sarcophagus. The lid is carved with the pharaoh's likeness — golden death mask, crossed crook and flail. Worth examining closely.
The lid is sealed with plaster. You'd need a tool to break the seal.
You chisel through the ancient plaster seal. The lid can now be pushed aside.
You push the massive lid. It grinds sideways, revealing the mummified remains of Pharaoh Khufu-Ankh and his burial goods. Among them, resting on the linen wrappings: the second cartouche seal.

objects.name: Canopic Jar Shelf
objects.description: Four canopic jars on a stone shelf.

then.text: The four sons of Horus guard the pharaoh's organs. Each jar lid is a different head: human, baboon, falcon, jackal. The baboon-headed jar (Hapy) has a slight crack.

You open the cracked baboon jar. Inside, wrapped in linen, is a crystal lens — polished quartz that refracts light. The ancients preserved it with the lungs, believing breath and light were connected.

objects.name: Wall Paintings
objects.description: Vibrant paintings depicting the pharaoh's life and afterlife journey.

then.text: The pharaoh's life in pigment. Birth, coronation, battles, building projects, and finally: the afterlife journey. In the final scene, five gods present five seals at a door. The door is painted with the same five cartouche slots you've seen elsewhere.

Through the lens, hidden pigments fluoresce! Behind the painted afterlife scene, a different image appears: the architect's escape route. A passage behind the false door! The architect left himself a way out.

objects.name: Treasure Pile
objects.description: Heaps of gold, jewelry, and precious artifacts.

then.text: Gold, lapis, carnelian, turquoise — a pharaoh's ransom. Among the treasures, you spot a golden ushabti servant figure and a bronze mirror. Worth taking?

objects.name: Guardian Alcove
objects.description: An empty alcove — something large stood here once.

then.text: A large alcove, empty. Bronze scratches on the floor show something massive once stood here — and recently walked out. Khepri's charging station? The alcove itself is deep enough to hide in.
You press into the alcove. The bronze scratches tell you this is where Khepri rests between patrols. Risky — but deeply hidden.

objects.name: False Door
objects.description: A carved stone door that doesn't open — or does it?

then.text: A carved stone door — a standard tomb feature. The ka (spirit) of the deceased passes through it. Not a real door. Or is it?
Now you know the truth — the architect built a real passage behind this false door. There must be a hidden mechanism.
You push. Solid stone. It's a false door — decorative, meant for the spirit world.

Knowing it's real, you search for the mechanism. A section of the carved border is slightly proud — a button! You press it. The false door swings inward, revealing a passage to the Water Channel room.
You probe the seams with the compass-chisel. A hidden mechanism clicks — the door pivots open! An engineer's path, bypassing the need to discover the secret through the paintings.

objects.name: Passage South
objects.description: The passage back to the Weighing Room.

then.text: You return to the Weighing Room.

objects.name: Sarcophagus Lid
objects.description: The heavy stone lid carved with the pharaoh's likeness.

then.text: The pharaoh's death mask stares up at you. Gold leaf over limestone. The plaster seal around the edges is ancient but breakable.

objects.name: Death Mask
objects.description: The golden death mask of Pharaoh Khufu-Ankh.

then.text: Serene golden features. The eyes are inlaid with obsidian and quartz. A masterwork of ancient craft.
You lift the death mask. It's lighter than expected — hollow gold over wood. Underneath: an inscription only the pharaoh was meant to read. A code for the treasury.

objects.name: Scroll Slot
objects.description: A narrow slot in the sarcophagus interior.

then.text: A slot for a scroll — the Book of the Dead was traditionally placed here. It's empty, but the slot itself has a false bottom.
You press the false bottom. Click. A small compartment opens, revealing a linen-wrapped strip.

objects.name: Linen Wrappings
objects.description: The mummy's linen bandages.

then.text: Layer upon layer of fine linen, still largely intact. Amulets and scarabs are woven throughout.

objects.name: Golden Ushabti Figure
objects.description: A solid gold servant figure among the burial treasures.

then.text: You pocket the golden ushabti. Heavy, solid gold. Worth a fortune — and possibly useful as a weight or offering.

objects.name: Lapis Amulet Box
objects.description: A box of carved lapis lazuli.

then.text: You open the box. Inside: protective amulets. One is shaped like an ivory wand — a hippo-ivory apotropaic wand used to ward off evil.

objects.name: Ivory Wand Display
objects.description: Where the ivory wand was kept.

then.text: An indentation where a curved wand once rested. Protective deities are carved into the stone shelf.

objects.name: Bronze Mirror Stand
objects.description: A lotus-shaped stand holding a polished bronze mirror.

then.text: You take the bronze mirror. Still reflective enough to redirect light.

objects.name: Architect's Desk
objects.description: A stone work desk covered in plans and tools.

then.text: The architect Senenmut's personal workspace. Covered in plans, measuring tools, ink pots, and papyrus. A rolled papyrus scroll sits prominently in the center.

objects.name: Tool Rack
objects.description: Racks of precision instruments and tools.

then.text: Copper chisels, measuring rods, plumb bobs, set squares. The toolkit of an ancient master builder. Most are too specialized, but one set catches your eye — a compass and reed pen set.
You take the architect's compass — a precision instrument with a sharp point.
You take a reed pen. Dried ink still clings to the tip.

objects.name: Clay Model
objects.description: A scale model of the tomb complex in clay.

then.text: A clay model of the entire tomb! You can see every chamber, every corridor, every trap. Khepri's patrol route is marked with bronze pins. The exit is at the northeast — through the Exit Corridor, past the Treasury.

objects.name: Measuring Instruments
objects.description: Ancient surveying and measuring tools.

then.text: A merkhet (plumb line for star alignment), a bay (surveying tool), and measuring cords. The merkhet could be useful in the Observatory.

objects.name: Papyrus Rack
objects.description: A wooden rack holding papyrus scrolls.

then.text: Construction records, worker schedules, supply lists. Most are too fragile to unroll. One scroll, however, is rolled tightly in a protective case — the architect's personal journal.
You carefully extract the protected scroll.

objects.name: Copper Forge
objects.description: A small forge for heating and shaping metal.

then.text: A small metallurgical forge. Charcoal still sits in the fire bed. Clay crucibles and bronze ingot molds line the shelf. If lit, it could heat metal for casting.
You light the charcoal with the oil-soaked fuse. It catches! The forge glows red. The heat is intense but focused — you could cast bronze or heat metal.
You melt the bronze gear in a crucible and pour it into a key-shaped mold you found on the shelf. A newly-cast bronze key, still warm. It matches the treasury chest lock.
Inside the mold was hidden: the third cartouche seal — Thoth, god of knowledge. The architect hid it where only a craftsman would find it.

objects.name: Stone Samples
objects.description: Labeled samples of different stone types.

then.text: Limestone, granite, alabaster, basalt. Each labeled in hieratic. The architect tested materials here.

objects.name: Workshop Wall (Water Channel)
objects.description: The far wall of the workshop.

then.text: According to the blueprints, a passage to the Water Channel room is behind this wall. There's a seam in the stone — another hidden door.
A featureless stone wall. Nothing interesting.
You press the seam. The wall pivots open, revealing a passage to the Water Channel room.
You step through into the Water Channel room. The sound of flowing water fills the corridor.

objects.name: Architect's Compass (on desk)
objects.description: A bronze compass on the desk.

then.text: The same compass symbol as on the pillar. This is the architect's signature tool.

objects.name: Reed Pen Set
objects.description: A set of sharpened reeds for writing.

then.text: Reed pens of various thicknesses. The finest one still has dried ink.

objects.name: Ink Wells
objects.description: Small stone wells containing pigmented inks.

then.text: Black (carbon), red (ochre), and blue (lapis) inks. The red and black have dried, but some blue ink remains liquid — preserved in its stone well.

objects.name: Unfinished Blueprint
objects.description: A half-drawn plan on the desk.

then.text: An unfinished plan for a new chamber. The architect was still working when the tomb was sealed. Notes in the margin: 'The water system feeds the Observatory lens. Without water pressure, the light cannot be focused.'

objects.name: Tomb Layout Plan
objects.description: A complete architectural plan of the tomb.

then.text: The complete tomb layout, drawn by the architect himself. Every room, passage, trap, and mechanism. Khepri's patrol route marked in red ink. The guardian follows a predictable circuit: Hall → Scarab → Weighing → Burial → back to Hall. A full circuit takes about 90 seconds.

objects.name: Water System Diagram
objects.description: Technical drawings of the tomb's hydraulic system.

then.text: The water system diagram: Valve A controls flow to the reservoir. Valve B controls flow to the Observatory. Open A first, then B, to build pressure. Opening B first floods the wrong chamber. The water wheel provides mechanical power to the Observatory lens.

objects.name: Gear Schematic
objects.description: Detailed plans of Khepri's internal mechanisms.

then.text: Khepri's internal schematics! The guardian runs on a clockwork mechanism powered by counterweights. Its weakness: the knee joints. Sand in the gears would slow it. Natron paste on the joints would corrode them. And a tripwire at knee height would topple it. The architect built in failsafes.

objects.name: Exit Route Notation
objects.description: The architect's personal escape plan.

then.text: 'My exit: through the Water Channel to the Observatory. Align the stars, redirect the light to the Treasury entrance. The Treasury connects to the Exit Corridor. The final door requires five cartouche seals — or the emergency release, which I alone know: behind the third cartouche slot, press and hold for ten heartbeats.'

objects.name: Main Water Channel
objects.description: A stone channel carrying flowing water from an underground spring.

then.text: Crystal-clear water flows through a precisely-cut stone channel. The ancient engineers tapped an underground spring. The water splits at two sluice gates — the flow must be managed to power the Observatory lens.

objects.name: Sluice Gate A (Reservoir)
objects.description: Controls water flow to the reservoir.

then.text: You open Sluice Gate A. Water flows into the reservoir, filling it steadily.

objects.name: Sluice Gate B (Observatory)
objects.description: Controls water flow to the Observatory.

then.text: With the reservoir pressurized, you open Gate B. Water surges through the pipe to the Observatory. The water wheel begins to turn — the lens mechanism has power!
You open Gate B but without pressure from the reservoir, only a trickle flows. Gate A must be opened first to build pressure.

objects.name: Water Wheel
objects.description: A bronze water wheel that converts flow into mechanical power.

then.text: A bronze water wheel, currently still. It needs pressurized water flow to turn. Gears connect it to a shaft leading upward — to the Observatory's lens mechanism.
The wheel spins steadily, powered by the redirected water. Gears turn, and you can hear the Observatory lens mechanism engaging above.

objects.name: Reservoir Pool
objects.description: A deep pool where water is stored.

then.text: A deep pool of clear water. Something glints at the bottom — a chest, submerged. The water is too deep to reach easily.

objects.name: Overflow Drain
objects.description: A drain that prevents the reservoir from overfilling.

then.text: The overflow drain. If opened, it would empty the reservoir — making the submerged chest accessible, but cutting water pressure to the Observatory.

You open the drain. Water rushes out, draining the reservoir. The submerged chest is now accessible — but the water wheel slows and stops. You'll need to close the drain and rebuild pressure if you need the Observatory.

objects.name: Stepping Stones
objects.description: A series of flat stones crossing the water channel.

then.text: Flat stones placed as stepping stones across the channel. They lead to the passage toward the Observatory.
You hop across the stepping stones and follow the passage to the Observatory.

objects.name: Submerged Chest
objects.description: A waterproof chest at the bottom of the reservoir.

then.text: With the reservoir drained, you pry open the waterproof chest. Inside: the fifth and final cartouche seal — Ra, the sun god. The architect hid it where only someone who understood the water system could reach it.
The chest is submerged in deep water. You can't reach it. The reservoir would need to be drained first.

objects.name: Valve Wheel A
objects.description: Controls water flow to the reservoir.

then.text: A bronze valve wheel. According to the diagram, this controls flow to the reservoir.

objects.name: Valve Wheel B
objects.description: Controls water flow to the Observatory.

then.text: A bronze valve wheel. This one controls flow to the Observatory lens mechanism.

objects.name: Flow Indicator
objects.description: A gauge showing water pressure.

then.text: The indicator shows full pressure. Water is flowing to the Observatory.
Pressure reads zero. The system needs water flow to both valves — A first for pressure, then B to direct it.

objects.name: Pipe Junction
objects.description: Where water pipes split in different directions.

then.text: Copper-lined stone pipes. The junction splits flow between the reservoir and the Observatory. Remarkable hydraulic engineering for 3000 years ago.

objects.name: Star Ceiling
objects.description: The vaulted ceiling painted with a precise star map.

then.text: A masterpiece of astronomical art. Every major constellation is mapped with gold paint on a deep blue ceiling. Orion's belt aligns with three marks on the alignment rings below. The star Sirius is painted largest, directly above the lens pedestal.

objects.name: Observation Platform
objects.description: A raised stone platform at the room's center.

then.text: A raised platform holding the lens apparatus. The alignment rings surround it. When everything is properly aligned and powered, the lens focuses light into a beam that can be directed through the exit passage.

objects.name: Lens Pedestal
objects.description: Where the crystal lens should be mounted.

then.text: An empty pedestal with a lens-shaped depression. The crystal lens from the Burial Chamber would fit here. When mounted with water power running the mechanism, the lens can be aligned to focus light.

objects.name: Alignment Rings
objects.description: Concentric bronze rings that rotate around the lens pedestal.

then.text: Three concentric bronze rings, each with constellation markers. They need to be rotated to align Orion, Sirius, and the Pleiades with their corresponding ceiling positions.

objects.name: Constellation Markers
objects.description: Bronze markers along the alignment rings.

then.text: Orion, Sirius, and the Pleiades — the three constellations that must be aligned with the star chart above.

objects.name: Zodiac Floor
objects.description: The floor is a massive zodiac circle.

then.text: A complete Egyptian zodiac carved into the floor. The twelve decans are marked with gold inlay. Beautiful, but decorative — the actual puzzle is in the alignment rings above.

objects.name: Light Beam Slot
objects.description: A narrow slot in the wall where the focused light beam exits.

then.text: A narrow slot leading to the Treasury entrance. When the lens is aligned and powered, focused light will pass through here, activating the Treasury's sun-powered lock.
A beam of focused light streams through the slot. The Treasury lock is now active.

objects.name: Orion
objects.description: The constellation Orion painted in gold.

then.text: Orion — Sah in Egyptian astronomy. The belt stars are marked with three dots in a line. The alignment ring's Orion marker must point to this position: 15 degrees from north.

objects.name: Sirius
objects.description: The star Sirius, painted brightest of all.

then.text: Sopdet — Sirius. The most important star in Egyptian astronomy. Its heliacal rising marked the New Year and the Nile flood. At zenith — directly overhead. The alignment ring must point straight up.

objects.name: Pleiades
objects.description: The Pleiades star cluster.

then.text: The Pleiades — seven stars in a cluster. The alignment ring marker must point to 45 degrees east.

objects.name: North Star Pointer
objects.description: A golden arrow pointing to the north celestial pole.

then.text: The reference point — north. All alignment measurements are relative to this marker.

objects.name: Lens Mount Point
objects.description: Where the crystal lens is mounted in the apparatus.

then.text: You mount the crystal lens in the apparatus. It clicks into place, perfectly sized. Now it needs water power and star alignment to focus the beam.

objects.name: Lens Housing
objects.description: The mechanical housing that holds and focuses the lens.

then.text: A precision bronze housing. When the lens is mounted and the water wheel turns, this housing slowly rotates, allowing fine focus adjustments.

objects.name: Angle Adjuster
objects.description: Fine adjustment controls for the lens angle.

then.text: Worm gear adjustment knobs. They control the lens angle with extreme precision.

objects.name: Focus Ring
objects.description: A ring that adjusts lens focal length.

then.text: The focus ring. When everything is aligned, turning this completes the beam focus.

objects.name: Gold Artifacts
objects.description: Heaps of golden artifacts.

then.text: A fortune in gold. Amulets, figurines, vessels, jewelry. Priceless beyond measure. But none of it helps you escape — it's just treasure.
You could stuff your pockets, but gold is heavy and makes noise. Focus on escape, not profit.

objects.name: Jeweled Chest
objects.description: An ornate chest inlaid with precious stones.

then.text: A gorgeous chest with a scarab-shaped lock. The numbers from the pillar inscription come to mind: 5-3-7-2. Worth examining the lock closely.

objects.name: Ceremonial Weapons
objects.description: Display rack of golden weapons — khopesh swords, spears, and maces.

then.text: Ceremonial weapons — gold-plated, beautiful, but too soft to be practical. A khopesh sword, a war mace, and ceremonial daggers. None would help against a bronze automaton.
You grab the khopesh. It bends in your hand — gold over wood. Ceremonial, not functional. Useless.

objects.name: Throne
objects.description: A golden throne — a replica of the pharaoh's seat of power.

then.text: The pharaoh's golden throne. Lions form the armrests. You could sit on it — or hide behind it.
You crouch behind the throne. The gold reflects torchlight, but you're well hidden.

objects.name: Trapped Floor
objects.description: A section of floor that looks slightly different.

then.text: You remember from the architect's plans — this floor section is a trap! Step on it and spikes deploy from the walls. It can be disarmed by pressing the tile sequence: left-right-center.

else.text: A section of floor that's slightly newer than the surrounding stone. Something about it feels wrong.

then.text: You press the disarm sequence: left-right-center. Click-click-click. The trap retracts. Safe to walk.
You step on the wrong tile. Bronze spikes shoot from the wall — you leap back just in time. Heart pounding.

objects.name: Exit to Corridor
objects.description: The passage leading from the Treasury to the Exit Corridor.

then.text: A sun-symbol door. It needs focused light from the Observatory to open — or it can be forced with enough leverage.
Light streams through the slot, hitting the sun symbol. The door is unlocked!
The sun-activated door opens. Beyond: the Exit Corridor. Daylight seeps through cracks. You're close.
You wedge the chisel into the door mechanism and lever with all your strength. The ancient lock shatters — brute force over elegance.
The door gives way. The Exit Corridor. Freedom is close.

objects.name: Offering Table
objects.description: A stone table for funerary offerings.

then.text: Dried offerings — grain, fruit (desiccated), and beer jars (long evaporated). The table itself has nothing useful.

objects.name: Chest Lock (Keypad)
objects.description: The scarab-shaped lock mechanism on the chest.

then.text: A four-symbol keypad built into the scarab lock. Hieratic numerals on each button — you need the right four-digit code.

objects.name: Chest Interior
objects.description: The contents of the jeweled chest.

then.text: The chest contains the pharaoh's most precious possession: a scroll of divine knowledge and — tucked beneath it — a cartouche seal.
You take the scroll and the cartouche seal. The scroll describes the Observatory alignment in detail — useful if you haven't figured it out yet.

objects.name: Hidden Compartment
objects.description: A false bottom in the chest.

then.text: The bottom of the chest feels hollow. A hidden compartment — classic tomb architecture.
You pry open the false bottom. Inside: a wrapped object. You unwrap it — a detailed miniature of Khepri, with joints that move. A blueprint in three dimensions.

objects.name: Scarab Key Slot
objects.description: A scarab-shaped depression in the chest.

then.text: The scarab amulet fits perfectly. Click — the chest unlocks from both the keypad side AND reveals the hidden compartment.

objects.name: Corridor Walls
objects.description: The walls of the exit corridor, covered in reliefs.

then.text: The final corridor. Reliefs depict the sun's journey across the sky. At the far end: the final door, and beside it — daylight! Cracks in the ceiling let sunlight stream in.

objects.name: Final Exit Door
objects.description: The last barrier between you and freedom.

then.text: The final door. Five cartouche-shaped slots are carved into its surface. Below them, barely visible, a small panel that might be an emergency release. 'Place the five seals of the gods to pass.'
Immovable. The five cartouche seals, or the emergency release — those are the only ways through.

objects.name: Guardian Track
objects.description: Bronze rails in the floor — Khepri's patrol track.

then.text: Bronze rails embedded in the floor. Khepri rolls along these during patrols. The tracks are worn smooth from centuries of use.
You stretch the tripwire across Khepri's track, anchored by the bronze gear. When the guardian rolls through, it will catch and topple. Khepri won't be coming back from this corridor for a while.

You smear the natron-oil paste across the track rails. When Khepri rolls through, the paste will coat its wheels and work into its joints. It won't stop immediately, but over its next few circuits, it will grind to a halt.

effects.text: From deep in the tomb, a grinding screech. Khepri's joints seize. The clicking stops. Silence, for the first time since you awoke.

objects.name: Daylight Crack
objects.description: Cracks in the ceiling letting in sunlight.

then.text: Sunlight. Real sunlight. The surface is right above you. Freedom is on the other side of that final door.
"HELP! I'M DOWN HERE!" Your voice echoes up through the cracks. But the tomb is in the middle of the desert. No one answers.

objects.name: Corridor Trap
objects.description: Another trapped floor section.

then.text: Another trap — the architect's plans warned about this one too. Same disarm sequence: left-right-center.
The floor looks odd here. Slightly different coloring. A trap?
You use the ivory wand to probe the floor ahead. The curved wand's reach lets you trigger the trap from a safe distance. Spikes deploy harmlessly.

objects.name: Lever Panel
objects.description: A panel of three levers near the exit.

then.text: Three levers. One is labeled with a sun, one with a moon, one with a star. A test — only the sun lever opens supplementary locks. The others trigger noise.
Knowing the architect's love of solar symbolism, you pull the sun lever. A lock disengages on the final door.

else.text: You pull a lever at random — the moon. A grinding sound, then a loud gong echoes through the tomb. Wrong choice.

objects.name: Door Seal
objects.description: The ancient seal on the exit door.

then.text: The royal seal. 'By decree of Pharaoh Khufu-Ankh: none shall pass without the five names of heaven.' The five cartouche slots below await their seals.

objects.name: Five-Seal Lock
objects.description: Five cartouche-shaped slots that require the five seals.

then.text: Five slots, each shaped for a specific cartouche seal. Khufu-Ankh, Imhotep, Thoth, Ma'at, Ra. Place all five and the door opens.
You place the Khufu-Ankh seal. It clicks into place. One of five.
The Imhotep seal slides home. Two of five.
Thoth's seal. Three of five.
Ma'at's seal. Four of five. One more.

Ra's seal — the last one. All five click into place simultaneously. The door mechanism engages. Ancient gears turn. The stone slab rises with thunderous grinding. Sunlight floods the corridor. You're free.

then.reason: You placed all five cartouche seals. The final door opens to blinding sunlight. You emerge into the desert, blinking, alive. Behind you, Khepri's clicks fade into silence. The Pharaoh's tomb keeps its treasures — but not its prisoner. You've earned passage through knowledge, craft, and truth.

objects.name: Individual Cartouche Slots
objects.description: The five individual seal positions.

then.text: Five cartouche slots in a row: Pharaoh, Architect, Wisdom, Truth, Sun. Each waits for its seal.

objects.name: Emergency Release
objects.description: A hidden mechanism behind the third cartouche slot.

then.text: A barely visible seam behind the third slot. Nothing you can do with it.
The architect's emergency release! Press and hold behind the third slot for ten heartbeats. No seals required.

You press the hidden button and hold. One... two... three... You count to ten, your heartbeat thundering. Click. The entire lock mechanism disengages. The door rises. Sunlight. The architect's secret escape works.

then.reason: Using the architect Senenmut's own emergency release — hidden behind the third cartouche slot — you bypass the five-seal lock entirely. The door opens to the desert. You escape not through divine approval, but through the architect's human ingenuity. His secret, kept for three millennia, saved your life.

then.text: You hold the forged decree to the door. Nothing. Of course — the door mechanism is purely mechanical. It can't read. But the attempt was creative.

on_solve.text: 5-3-7-2. The lock clicks open. Inside: scrolls and a hidden compartment.

on_fail.text: Wrong code. The mechanism resets with a click.

on_solve.text: The alignment rings click into place. Sirius at zenith! The crystal lens focuses a beam of light that streams through the exit slot toward the Treasury. The sun-powered lock activates.

on_fail.text: The rings grind but don't lock. Wrong alignment.

config.correct_step_message: Click. The tile sinks into place.
config.wrong_step_message: The tiles spring back. Wrong order.

on_solve.text: The mosaic shudders and sinks, revealing a hidden compartment. Inside: the first cartouche seal — Khufu-Ankh!

on_fail.text: The tiles reset with a series of clicks.

on_solve.text: Gates A and B open, drain closed. Water pressure builds and flows to the Observatory. The water wheel engages!

on_fail.text: Water floods the wrong channel. Pipes groan in protest.

on_solve.text: 3-7-1-4-9. The combination lock behind the emergency panel disengages. A secondary bypass!

on_solve.reason: You cracked the combination lock hidden behind the emergency release panel. The clay shard you found in the rubble — the very first item you picked up — held the answer all along. The door opens. Sunlight floods in. You are free.

on_fail.text: The dials click, but nothing happens. Wrong combination.

phases.name: Awakening

on_enter.text: Dust. Darkness. Pain. You fell through the floor of the upper tomb into sealed chambers below. As your eyes adjust, you hear it — click... click... click... — the rhythmic sound of ancient machinery. Something is moving in the corridors. Something that has been moving for three thousand years.

phases.ambient_text: Distant clicking echoes through stone corridors. Dust motes drift in faint light.

phases.name: Exploration

on_enter.text: Torchlight reveals the scale of this place. Ten chambers of ancient engineering surround you. And in the corridors between them, Khepri patrols — an automaton that never tires, never sleeps, and never forgives intrusion.

phases.ambient_text: Clicking grows closer, then recedes. Khepri patrols the corridors in a tireless circuit.

phases.name: Guardian Alert

on_enter.text: The clicking accelerates. Khepri has detected significant disturbance. The guardian's patrol tightens — it's searching specifically for you now. Its bronze head swivels, obsidian eyes scanning. Be very, very careful.

phases.ambient_text: Rapid clicking. Bronze scraping on stone. Khepri is hunting.

phases.name: Final Trial

on_enter.text: You can see daylight. The exit corridor is open. But Khepri stands between you and freedom. One final gauntlet — navigate the corridor, avoid the traps, reach the door. This is the architect's final trial.

phases.ambient_text: Sunlight ahead. Bronze clicking behind. Almost free.

effects.text: Click... click... click... The sound is closer now. Something metal, something heavy, walking on stone. A mechanical rhythm, older than any clock.
Sand shifts somewhere above. The tomb is not entirely stable — your fall weakened the ceiling. Time is not infinite here.

Through a doorway, you catch a glimpse — bronze legs, scarab-shaped body, obsidian eyes that glow faintly red. Khepri passes through the Hall of Pillars on its endless circuit. It's enormous, and its footsteps are precisely timed.
A deep tremor shakes the tomb. Dust cascades from the ceiling. The structure is weakening. You need to find the exit before the tomb collapses entirely.
The water system rumbles. With the valves open, pressure has built throughout the tomb's hydraulic network. You hear distant mechanisms engaging — the observatory lens can now be powered.

Khepri enters the Burial Chamber and stops. Its head swivels to the open sarcophagus. A low mechanical growl — gears grinding in what almost sounds like anger. The guardian has seen the desecration. It will search harder now.
A massive crack splits the ceiling of the Antechamber. The entire tomb is shifting. Stone groans. You don't have much longer.
Khepri's patrol route is erratic now. Grinding, lurching steps replace the precise clicking. The natron paste is working — the guardian is corroding from within.

killer.name: Khepri
killer.description: An ancient mechanical guardian — a bronze scarab automaton the size of a large dog, running on clockwork gears and counterweight mechanisms. It has patrolled these corridors for over three thousand years without stopping.

on_approach: Click... click... click... The rhythm quickens.
Bronze scrapes on stone. Getting closer.
The red glow of obsidian eyes appears in the corridor.
on_search: Khepri's head rotates slowly, scanning. Bronze feelers extend from its scarab shell.
The automaton probes each shadow, each alcove. Methodical. Tireless.
Click-click-click-click — rapid scanning. Khepri knows you're here.
on_clear: Khepri's head retracts. The clicking resumes its slow, steady rhythm. It moves on.
The bronze guardian turns and rolls away. For now.
The red glow fades down the corridor. Safe. Barely.
on_evidence: Khepri stops at the disturbed area. Its head tilts. Gears grind — processing. Anger?
The automaton discovers the change. Bronze feelers probe the evidence. The clicking intensifies.
A mechanical screech — Khepri has found proof of intrusion. It will search harder now.
on_catch: Khepri's bronze arms seize you. Three thousand years of mechanical patience, and the guardian has finally found its prey. The tomb keeps what enters.

effects.text: Khepri noticed the open false door. The guardian sealed it shut again. You'll need to reopen it.
Khepri's heavy treads sweep the oil from the channels. The fuel is dispersed.

special_behaviors.description: Khepri avoids the fire-filled corridors. Its bronze body conducts heat and warps the gears.
Khepri hits the tripwire and topples. It takes 90 seconds to right itself.
The corrosive paste eats into Khepri's joints. Movement slows, then stops.

win_conditions.description: Place all five cartouche seals in the exit door.
Use the architect's emergency release behind the third cartouche slot.
Enter the combination from the clay shard on the hidden lock.

lose_conditions.description: Khepri finds you during a search.
The tomb collapses after too much time.

hints.text: Search the rubble where you fell. Your first tools are buried there.
The torch needs a spark. Strike metal against stone.
The alcove in the Antechamber hides a golden key.
The hieroglyph wall hides secrets visible only through a lens. Find the crystal in the Burial Chamber.
The architect left his mark on the fourth pillar. If you know his symbol, press it three times.
Read the confessions first, then place the feather. Ma'at judges honesty, not weight.
Open Gate A first to build pressure, then Gate B to direct flow to the Observatory.
Five seals, one door. But the architect always left himself a back door. Look for his notes in the workshop.
Khepri's weakness is in its joints. Sand, natron, or a tripwire could slow or stop it.

solution_paths.name: The Scholar's Path
solution_paths.description: Solve puzzles through knowledge and observation. Minimal noise, maximum understanding.
steps: Search rubble → get clay_shard + copper_chisel
Light torch with chisel → reveals hieroglyphs
Read hieroglyph wall → learn tomb layout and seal locations
Find scarab amulet in alcove → open north door to Hall of Pillars
Read pillar inscriptions → learn star alignment code
Use crystal lens on hieroglyphs → find hidden messages about workshop
Open workshop via fourth pillar → explore architect's workspace
Study blueprints → learn water system and Khepri's weaknesses
Follow water system to Observatory → align stars
Focused light opens Treasury → find remaining seals
Place all five cartouche seals → escape through final door

solution_paths.name: The Engineer's Path
solution_paths.description: Manipulate the tomb's mechanical systems. Use the architect's tools and knowledge of machines.
steps: Search rubble → get clay_shard + copper_chisel
Light torch → explore
Find workshop through pillar mechanism
Study gear schematics → understand Khepri's weaknesses
Forge bronze key at workshop → gain cartouche seal 3
Manage water system → power Observatory
Build sabotage gear or tripwire trap from bronze gear + sand/wire
Disable Khepri with trap or corrosive paste
Navigate to exit with guardian disabled
Use emergency release OR combination lock from clay shard to escape

solution_paths.name: The Warrior's Path
solution_paths.description: Brute force through obstacles. Loud, fast, risky — but direct.
